note: Trigger function that copies customer_id into the new bigint column on every insert / update of customer_id. Touches no table, takes no lock on orders.

In one short transaction: add the nullable bigint column (metadata only, no rewrite), an unvalidated NOT NULL check, and the sync trigger. From the commit on, every new row has customer_id_new set. The brief ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock is taken with a 500ms lock_timeout and retried, so app queries never queue behind it for long.
Backfill ids up to 2,000,000 in batches of 10,000 rows, committing after each batch (row locks only; the app only inserts, so nothing contends).
Vacuum so the dead row versions from this chunk are reused by the next one (keeps bloat bounded). Non-blocking for the app.
Backfill everything above 8,000,000 up to the current max id (rows inserted after the trigger was created already have the value).

Validate the NOT NULL check (SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE: app reads and inserts keep running), then verify every row has customer_id_new equal to customer_id. Fails the plan, before any destructive change, if a single row differs.

The swap, in one short transaction with lock_timeout + retry: SET NOT NULL (no table scan: proven by the validated check), drop the trigger, drop the old integer column (metadata only), rename the bigint column to customer_id, drop the helper check. The app's SQL names columns explicitly, so it works unchanged before and after; no redeploy needed.
Drop the trigger function and check the result: orders.customer_id is bigint NOT NULL.
Statistics for the new customer_id column (used by the /customer query planner).
